items.note: In the cream footer with its rising arc, the invalid email field has a 2px danger border, and below it sits a solid alert glyph with a short red message saying what to type. The ink Subscribe pill sits on its ledge beside it. This follows the reference's form treatment (09, 11) and clearly says what went wrong and how to fix it.

At night the footer is an indigo band with a wave, and the error field keeps a visible red border and red message on navy. The white pill matches the reference's night palette (03). Still clear, with the same careful treatment as the light version.

The red message and alert glyph are there under the field, with a full-width ink pill. But the email input is squashed to a thin sliver, far shorter than the pill under it, so the errored field the message points to barely reads as a field. The reference keeps its inputs full control height.

The form is replaced by one line of body text with a tiny tick and a small crescent-and-sparkle. It is readable, but small and flat for the system. The spec's confirmation is an ink pill toast, or a composition with an orbiting sparkle. The reference states outcomes with bolder, more confident shapes.
Same small crescent-and-tick line of text on the indigo footer band. It is legible on navy, but as underplayed as the light version against the system's confident confirmations.

The phone capture has the same small inline confirmation in the footer: a tiny glyph and a sentence. It is clear what happened, but the confirmation has none of the presence the reference gives its moments.

The empty result is a big yolk radius-xl panel with an h4 title, a one-line hint and an ink Clear filters pill. That is right in hue, type and action, and easy to understand. But the only art is a lone ~40px blue blob, a single small mark. The reference would fill a panel like this with a full composition or a large glyph.
At night it is the same yolk panel with the same lone small blue blob and a white pill. The structure is clear, but the art is as thin as in the light version.

Stacked well on the phone: focused search with a blue ring, wrapped filter pills, a yolk panel with title, hint and ink pill. The lone small blob is still the only art. Further down, the footer's email input is squashed to a thin sliver.

The focused nav link gets a flush, square blue outline that touches the yellow nav dot, with no offset or rounding. The reference's ring follows the pill's shape 2px out (11). This is the same gap named last round, still open.
At night the ring is yellow and easy to see on navy, but it is still a flush square box around the nav link, not a rounded ring 2px out like the reference's.
On the phone the square blue box around the current nav link is oversized and flush with the label's edge, cruder than the reference's shaped ring.

Post covers now each have their own readable subject: a document, a flag, stacked pills, a clock, an open box and a moon with sparkles. That is a clear step up from the hue-swapped formula last round. Most are flat with little crescent shading. The confetti disc is split by a straight diagonal like a pie, and the hero disc floats away from its cards, where the reference shapes overlap in one tight cluster.

The header band holds one cluster: a crescent-shaded blue hexagon, an overlapping pink pill and a tucked white dot, all inside the band. The inline figure is a clean card-of-swatches pictogram. Close to the reference's flat shape kit, with only slightly less character.

This band's cluster is laid out differently: a large blue blob, an overlapping white disc and a pink sparkle. The inline figure shows two pages side by side and reads as release notes. Each drawing is its own and built to the recipe, close to the reference's crops.

A sun-behind-cloud cover on blue, a book pictogram with a sparkle on a cream plate, and initials avatars on crescent discs in category hues. All are readable, distinct and within the shape kit. The plate pictogram is a bit small for its plate next to the reference's 07.

The motion matches the spec: a slow 8s drift on the hero disc, a 750ms build with cards fading in one after another, staggered fade-ins for the confetti and the plate. The vignette's third card is a typing bubble with pop dots that empties into a blank white pill after the build. In static captures it stays a faint, empty ghost strip in the hero.

findings.summary: Nav-link focus is still a flush square outline with no offset, touching the current-page dot. The reference's ring follows the control's rounded shape 2px out. This gap was named last round and has not closed.
The empty search result has the right panel, title and ink pill, but its only art is a lone ~40px blob. The spec and reference call for a full composition or a large glyph.

The newsletter confirmation is one line of body text with a tiny tick and crescent. The system's confirmation is an ink pill toast, or a composition with an orbiting sparkle, so this success state is underplayed next to the reference's confident moments.

Drawings are now distinct and readable, but most covers are flat with no crescent shading. The confetti two-color disc is split by a straight diagonal like a pie chart, where the reference lays a curved second shape over the disc. The home hero disc, sparkle and dot float apart from the cards instead of forming one overlapping cluster.
On phones the footer's email input collapses to a thin sliver, much shorter than its pill, so the field (and in the error state the errored field) barely reads as an input.
The hero vignette's third card is a typing bubble whose pop dots empty out after the build, leaving a blank white pill. In static captures it stays a faint, empty ghost strip under the other cards.
